Hi Maya,

Thanks for taking this—attached is our first-pass draw.io export of the private VPC topology we discussed. A few things we want your input on before we commit to cross-connects and the control plane endpoints: 

- Control plane placement: can Redwood support a split control plane (hosted control signals) while the data plane stays entirely on-prem? Any operational tradeoffs?
- Egress paths: we need to ensure tenant inference traffic never leaves our subnet except for metrics/telemetry. What's the recommended pattern for KV cache and model artifact fetches?
- HA/cutover: if we fail over between colo racks, do you recommend mirroring runtime state or relying on a permissive cold-start?

We're hoping for a short readout and recommended minimal changes to our sketch. Attaching: acme_vpc_sketch_v1.drawio.pdf (diagram), plus a CSV of IP allocations (not attached here).

From: maya_srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>

Hanna — thanks for the sketch, very helpful. Quick readout below; I added a reference slide deck (attached) with a compact topology for your ops team.

High-level recommendations:
- Control plane: host the control plane in Redwood-managed cloud endpoints (region us-west-2) and expose a signed, mTLS-protected control channel. This keeps rollout and versioning simple while ensuring the data plane (GPU nodes) stays inside Acme’s VPC.
- Artifact fetches & model telemetry: use an outbound-only, whitelisted S3 endpoint (or equivalent) in your colo; model artifacts should be pulled via a pre-authorized pull proxy inside the tenant subnet to avoid direct egress. KV/prefix caching remains local to the runtime (no outbound).
- Egress / telemetry: send aggregated telemetry via an observability forwarder that posts to a Redwood collector endpoint over mTLS; sample events to reduce bandwidth. No inference tokens should traverse public internet.
- HA: recommend state snapshot + warm-restart pattern. Mirror lightweight KV metadata to a co-located NFS or small key-value store with async replication — avoids long cold starts and keeps tail latency acceptable.

Open questions for your team:
- Can you place a small NAT/proxy in the tenant DMZ that allows egress to our collector endpoints only?
- Do you have a colo-side PKI we can anchor for mTLS certs? If not, we can support short-lived certs via your KMS.

Next steps: I propose a focused runbook & acceptance criteria doc we can agree on, then a short on-site topology review. I attached the quick reference (redwood_acme_ref_arch_v1.pdf).

Available for a 30-min sync Friday 10–12 PST; please pick a slot.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple of low-level constraints from runtime + ops:

> On 2026-08-18 18:04, maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai wrote:
> > - Artifact fetches & model telemetry: use an outbound-only, whitelisted S3 endpoint...
> > - HA: recommend state snapshot + warm-restart pattern.

Notes:
- BGP vs static: prefer BGP for multi-rack failover at colo; if BGP is not possible, we can do static routes but risk longer cutovers.
- NAT placement: NAT should live in a minimal egress zone that allows only two destinations: your S3 artifact bucket and our collector endpoint (both mTLS + IP allowlist).
- Firewall rules: explicitly deny all ingress to the runtime plane; allow SSH/management only from the control-plane proxy IPs.
- Observability: instrument token-level redaction in the forwarder; we can provide a small binary that runs as the forwarder if you prefer to avoid cloud egress libraries.

I'll draft a short ops checklist (runbook) and upload to the ACME drive. Also recommend we include a brief test plan for canary traffic (1% of production traffic for 24h).

-priyom
Priyom Das
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hanna — thanks, this is actionable. Confirming next steps and acceptance criteria below so ops teams have a clear checklist before we schedule the on-site: 

Proposed acceptance checklist (minimal):
- Control channel: mTLS handshake succeeds between Acme proxy and Redwood control endpoint; cert rotation tested once.
- Artifact fetch: model artifact pulled from whitelisted S3 proxy with file checksum validation.
- Egress policy: runtime plane cannot initiate any outbound connection except to the NAT/proxy; verified by packet capture on two sample nodes.
- Canary traffic: 1% sample traffic routed to the setup for 24h with latency and error SLAs recorded.
- Failover: simulate rack failover; warm-restart recovers with <5s additional P50 latency.

Operational items & schedule:
- Priyom will upload the ops runbook and proposed firewall/route snippets by COB tomorrow.
- Maya & I will join your on-site review Tuesday 2026-08-24; please confirm room and network access.
- We will request a short proof-of-concept slot on colo for the canary during the week of 2026-09-07.
